key_insight: Lighthouse RL improves sample efficiency in analog circuit sizing by restarting training from strong intermediate solutions instead of repeatedly exploring from scratch. This helps RL focus on promising regions of the design space and adapt better to different performance targets.
problem_solved: The paper addresses two core issues in analog circuit optimization: poor generalization across changing performance targets and wasted samples spent exploring low-value or unpromising regions during RL training.
method: Use reinforcement learning for analog circuit sizing, but periodically reset episodes from high-performing configurations discovered during training.
Treat these strong configurations as "lighthouses" that guide exploration toward more promising areas of the design space.
Improve sample efficiency by reducing time spent on ineffective exploration and reusing good partial solutions.
Enable better adaptation to varied performance targets compared with conventional optimization strategies.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how carefully designed reset strategies can make RL far more efficient in expensive real-world optimization tasks. It is especially relevant for domains like hardware design where each trial is costly and sample budgets are limited.
